newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Algerian jailed in Belgium starts hunger strike.
newsitem.headline: Algerian jailed in Belgium starts hunger strike.

text.p: Algerian Ahmed Zaoui, convicted in Belgium of playing a central role in a criminal network here, has started a hunger strike against his detention, the Algerian Islamic Salvation Front (FIS) said on Monday.
"Zaoui starts a hunger strike today against his illegal detention (in Belgium) since October 3, 1995," FIS said in a statement.

Zaoui, a member of FIS, was sentenced to four years in prison in November 1995. He and several other North Africans were tried on charges which included possession of forged documents and illegal possession and transportation of arms and explosives.

Most of the sentence was suspended, technically freeing Zaoui, but the Belgian Interior Ministry has kept him in jail while his request for political ayslum is being processed on the grounds that he is a potential danger to the public.
Belgian authorities believe Zaoui is a leading member of the fundamentalist Algerian Armed Islamic Group (GIA), a charge he has denied.

GIA has claimed responsibility for killing hundreds of people in the wave of violence which has swept Algeria since early 1992, when the authorities cancelled a general election in which the banned FIS took a huge lead.
An Interior Ministry spokesman told Reuters on Monday that Zaoui's second asylum request had recently been rejected. A first request was rejected last year.
"We are looking for a solution," the spokesman said.
He reiterated that Zaoui would not be deported to Algeria, where he is under sentence of death.
